subject: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra
messages:
From: Anna Torres <anna@lyraanalytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: michael.dunn@lyraanalytics.com, procure@lyraanalytics.com
Date: 2026-08-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Lyra’s execs liked Redwood’s latency profile, but procurement asked for a deeper comparison vs our incumbent (CloudFoundryAI) focused on: unit price parity, one-time onboarding effort, and any operational workarounds that would increase their TCO.

Can you share a simple economic side-by-side and the realistic list of non-recurring engineering (NRE) or integration tasks we should budget for? They specifically call out: model compatibility risks, KV cache migration, and any ACL/KMS adjustments.

I attached our SOW and current utilization curve. We’re on an aggressive timeline — procurement wants a concrete counter to present in their vendor short-list meeting next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Anna Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships | Lyra Analytics
Attachment: Lyra_RFP_v2.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Anna Torres <anna@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra

Anna — really appreciate the clear ask and RFP. I looped in Marcus (solutions) and Tessa (AE/pricing) to pull together a short packet — high-level econ + ops lift and one proposed concession we can take to procurement.

Short answers up front:
- Unit parity: we can match effective per-token economics with a blended 12-month prepay + usage credit structure for your volume band (see Marcus’s calc coming next).
- Onboarding: expect ~3–5 engineering sprints (2–3 weeks each) of effort if you move KV cache and custom scoring hooks; we can reduce that with a small upfront integration credit and dedicated SE time.
- Security/KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; there’s an initial config and audit (~2–4 business days) but no long-term friction.

We’ll send the spreadsheet and a counter offer PDF within the hour.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Anna Torres <anna@lyraanalytics.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra

Anna / team — attached is a concise cost model and ops-friction worksheet comparing Redwood vs CloudFoundryAI given the utilization in your RFP. Key rows I highlighted: 1) steady-state per-token cost after quant/ batching, 2) expected one-time SE hours for KV migration, 3) estimated latency delta at 1k concurrent sessions.

Notes:
- We assume you adopt our recommended quantization profile; if you require lossless FP16 the per-token gap widens (~6–8%).
- Onboarding hours: 120–200 hours (3–5 sprints) for a typical mid-size deployment — we priced an SE day at our standard rate but are happy to convert to a credit.

Attachment: redwood_cost_vs_cfai.xlsx

I left comment flags on the sheets where we made conservative assumptions. If you want, I can strip the sheet down into a single-page executive summary for procurement.

—Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Anna Torres <anna@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra

Anna — following up with a targeted commercial proposal to take to procurement. Highlights:
- 12-month blended prepay: 20% upfront prepay + 10% usage credit across the first 6 months for volumes in your band (effective 18% uplift vs list).
- Integration credit: $30k in SE credits applied to onboarding (converts to ~150 SE hours).
- Implementation SLA: dedicated SE + 2-week canary window; rollback plan and fallthrough to incumbent model for first 30 days.

I attached the formal counter (RNW_counter_offer_Lyra.pdf) and callout doc for the procurement slide. If procurement needs a purchase order-ready line-item, we’ll generate one.

Quick ask: can procurement confirm they’ll need a term-sheet (legal) or a PO-only acceptance? That changes how we route internal approvals.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: RNW_counter_offer_Lyra.pdf
From: Anna Torres <anna@lyraanalytics.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: michael.dunn@lyraanalytics.com, procure@lyraanalytics.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime parity, packaging & onboarding lift — Lyra

Team — thanks, this is exactly what procurement wanted to see. A few procurement notes:
- They prefer a PO-only acceptance if there are no legal material changes. We’ll confirm today.
- Can you send the one-page econ summary Marcus mentioned and a bullet list of the 5 highest-risk integration tasks (so they can tuck contingency into the PO)?

Assuming PO flow is acceptable, we’ll aim to present your counter in the vendor short-list meeting tomorrow and circle back with a PO or list of redline asks. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Anna
Head of Platform Partnerships | Lyra Analytics
